descriptionInUI: Runtime for GPS denial. Inert unless the mission generator emits dcsRetribution.gpsJamming (the 'GPS jamming' setting is on and a live GPS-jamming ground site exists). DCS models no GPS receiver, so the effect is scripted on the WEAPON: a satellite-guided store (JDAM, JSOW, JASSM, SLAM-ER, KAB-500S -- never laser, TV or IR weapons) released into a live jammer's bubble is tracked in flight, then destroyed just short of impact and detonated a scored distance off the aimpoint. The bomb visibly goes long; the deeper inside the bubble, the further off. Real ordnance from a real jet: this script spawns nothing and owns no kills beyond producing the miss explosion, and killing the jammer restores accuracy immediately. Symmetric -- a site degrades the OPPOSING side's weapons only. The firing flight gets one cue the first time a weapon of theirs is spoofed, so a failed pass reads as jamming rather than as a bug.

specificOptions.nameInUI: Chance a weapon inside the bubble is degraded (%)
specificOptions.descriptionInUI: Rolled ONCE per weapon, the first tick it is inside a live jammer's reach. Below 100 some stores get through, so a package can still score hits inside a jammed area.

specificOptions.nameInUI: Terminal altitude the spoofed weapon is destroyed at (ft AGL)
specificOptions.descriptionInUI: The weapon flies its whole normal profile and is removed only this low, so the pilot sees the release, the fall and the detonation -- just in the wrong place.

specificOptions.nameInUI: Fallback miss explosion power (kg TNT eq)
specificOptions.descriptionInUI: Used ONLY for a weapon that does not report its own warhead (a mod store with a thin descriptor). Everything else detonates with its real warhead, scaled below.

specificOptions.nameInUI: Miss detonation size, as % of the weapon's own warhead
specificOptions.descriptionInUI: The miss detonates with the store's REAL explosive mass, so a 2000 lb JDAM craters like one and a 500 lb JDAM does not. 100 = the full warhead, which is what a bomb landing off-target actually does; lower it if you want a jammed pass to be less destructive than a clean miss.

specificOptions.nameInUI: Announce the first spoofed weapon to the firing flight

specificOptions.descriptionInUI: Keep small. The terminal gate is predictive (it fires when the weapon would be through the floor by the NEXT sample), so a coarse step only makes the destroy happen higher, never later than impact.

specificOptions.nameInUI: Give up tracking a released weapon after (s)
